entries.title: Logan Beats Logan, Joe Loses To Joe, And Nobody Knows Who To Hate
entries.subtitle: A night so incestuous the draft sheet needed a lie-down and a cold flannel
entries.html:
Gather round, you six glorious degenerates, for the Night of Thursday 25 June served up the rarest delicacy in all of sweepstake gastronomy: men forced to cheer and weep in the same breath, owners playing tennis against the mirror, brothers circling like the opening pages of Genesis. I nearly required defibrillation in the kitchen.

Group E: Logan v Logan, the civil war of one man's soul

In the fixture that should have been refereed by a therapist, Ecuador 🇪🇨 beat Germany 🇩🇪 2-1 — both, of course, the property of Logan, who watched his fifth seed knife his second seed and somehow won the argument with himself. Germany still strolls through top; Ecuador now waits, sweating, in the best-third lottery, neither in nor out, a man holding a raffle ticket in purgatory. Meanwhile Joe's Ivory Coast 🇨🇮 thumped Barney's Curaçao 🇨🇼 2-0, sending the Elephants surging into the knockouts and consigning poor Curaçao — minus-eight goal difference, the footballing equivalent of a wet weekend in Skegness — to the abyss bar a miracle.

Group F: the all-Joe horror show

I must report on myself with the cold detachment of a coroner. Tunisia 🇹🇳 1-3 Netherlands 🇳🇱 was Joe versus Joe versus Joe, and the Dutch duly battered my own Tunisians into a fine paste — Netherlands top of the group, Tunisia bottom with nil points and a goal difference of minus-TEN, the worst surname I own. And Japan 🇯🇵 1-1 Sweden 🇸🇪 saw Logan's Japan qualify while my Sweden slumps to third and the same anxious lottery vigil. So I both prospered and perished, repeatedly, all night. I am a one-man tragicomedy.

Group D: heroism, futility, and a goalless shrug

Paraguay 🇵🇾 0-0 Australia 🇦🇺 — Barney's bore-draw was enough to send Geo's Socceroos through in second, while Paraguay drops to third and the waiting room. And in the night's most magnificently pointless act of valour, Sean's Turkey 🇹🇷 beat Pete's USA 🇺🇸 3-2 — a win so glorious and so utterly useless it deserves a plaque: Turkey are OUT regardless, and the USA had ALREADY qualified. Sean burned the house down to roast a single marshmallow.

The reckoning

Now to the gold. Joe hoovered up a table-topping 7 sweepstake points on the night — more than anyone — and dragged Ivory Coast to the summit of League 4, dethroning Barney's Canada. Self-loathing pays, apparently. But the £60 headline is fratricidal: Logan went into the night second and leaves it TOP of the player league, level on 36 with brother-betrayer's-luck, while Geo — who led coming in — managed a measly point from his goalless Aussies and got leapfrogged into second on the very same 36. Two men, identical scores, one crown; the Cain-and-Abel of it all writes itself, except neither is my brother tonight, so I'll simply enjoy it. Pete got precisely nothing, watched his qualified Americans get done by an already-doomed Turkey, and remains rooted to the bottom like a barnacle of sorrow. Geo top of Leagues 1, 2, 3 and 6 — fine, fine, the swot. But on the night it's Logan's crown and Joe's quiet, masochistic surge. Sleep well, lads. I shan't.

entries.title: Geo Goes Full Pharaoh as His Brother Watches From the Cheap Seats
entries.subtitle: Nine points, three leagues toppled, and an all-Geo civil war that he literally could not lose
entries.html:
Gather round, you six gilded fools, for last night the heavens parted over the group stages and rained down a biblical quantity of sweepstake points onto one smug, fraternal head. Geo — who waltzed into the evening in second and swaggered out of it top of the £60 league on 35 points — had the kind of night that makes brothers stop speaking at Christmas. And his actual brother, Joe, yours truly, your humble impresario, sat motionless in fourth with not a single team playing, watching the family silverware get burgled in real time. Marvellous.

Group A — the Geo Civil War

It takes a special man to engineer a fixture he cannot lose, and behold: 🇿🇦 South Africa beat 🇰🇷 South Korea 1-0 in a match where Geo owned both dugouts, gaining points with one hand whatever the other did. Meanwhile 🇲🇽 Mexico (Geo, naturally) put 🇨🇿 Czechia (Logan) to the sword 3-0 to finish a flawless three-from-three on nine points — and in doing so dethroned Germany at the summit of the grand League 1 AND League 2. South Korea now lingers third, sweating on the best-third lottery; Czechia, bless it, is all but cremated.

Group B — Switzerland soars, Qatar sinks

🇨🇭 Switzerland (Geo, who else) saw off 🇨🇦 Canada 2-1 to top the group on seven and seize the lead in League 3 from Colombia. Spare a thought, though, for Geo's other Group B horse: 🇶🇦 Qatar was dismantled 3-1 by 🇧🇦 Bosnia-Herzegovina, handing Logan the points and the leadership of League 7. So even on his coronation night Geo had a team bottom of the pile on minus-eight goal difference. Greedy bastard can't even fail tidily.

Group C — Logan's Brazilian-Moroccan double act

While Geo plundered, Logan quietly matched him for nine points and climbed from third to second in the player league. 🇧🇷 Brazil strolled past 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Scotland 3-0, and 🇲🇦 Morocco saw off 🇭🇹 Haiti 4-2 — both Logan teams topping Group C on seven apiece. For poor Sean, Scotland's 0-3 capitulation was the footballing equivalent of being shown the door of your own party; the Tartan lads cling to a third-place prayer. And Pete? Haiti are out, played three lost three, and Pete is rooted to the bottom of the player league with the dead-eyed look of a man who drafted with his heart.

The Reckoning

So let the record show: this was Geo's night, top to bottom, a +9 heist that vaulted him from second to first and left him leading Leagues 1, 2 and 3 like some moustachioed cartel boss. Logan matched the haul to slot into second, the only man keeping the thing a contest. The real carnage, though, was Barney — top of the player league coming in, knocked down to third without kicking a ball, a man relegated by other people's brilliance. Joe stays fourth, dignified and irrelevant. Sean clings to fifth on Scottish hope, and Pete brings up the rear. One brother is feasting; the other is writing about it. There is a lesson there somewhere, and I refuse to learn it.
